title: Which record owns the scan of STEGO's own Go modules for known vulnerabilities?
description: The workflows check STEGO's own dependencies: go mod verify and govulncheck in checks.yml and runtime-library.yml, and vulnerability-scan.yml (ST-ASR-TOOL06), which scans every Go module on main each week. No design record asks for this, so no test of it can be a proof: the test of the module list in scripts/test_release_publishing.py names no record. Options: (a) a new rule of ST-STD-TRUST: every Go module of STEGO MUST be verified against its go.sum and scanned for known vulnerabilities by each check of the module and on main each week, and a reachable known vulnerability MUST fail the check; its test is the module list test; (b) a UC requirement of an Assuring use case; (c) keep it as tooling with no proof. Recommendation: (a): it is an engineering rule for STEGO's own code, as the rules of ST-STD-TRUST are, and it holds the scan to every module, also one added later.

title: Where does stego build download take the runtime pin of a service, while the runtime library is not released on the public module proxy?
description: Since the archetype move (ST-SUP-RC20-OC39) every generated service imports the runtime library, and the examples do too. stego deps and local builds resolve the pin from the common registry's runtime folder, verified by the pinned hash (ST-SUP-INV10). stego build download runs in a fixed environment with the public module proxy only, and a module that the proxy cannot supply stops it (ST-BLD-UC02-R03). The runtime is not released: no tag registry/runtime/<version> is pushed and stego.dev serves no go-import page for it, so the application build job of CI stops at github.com/jsell-rh/stego/registry/runtime v0.30.0. Options: (a) the Product owner releases the runtime at each pin: serve the go-import page, push the tag registry/runtime/<version> at the commit whose folder hashes to the pin, and the public proxy then supplies it; (b) stego build download takes the pin from the common registry's runtime folder as stego deps does, as a local file proxy before the public proxy, only when the folder hashes to the pinned sum, and the build record names that source; (c) the application build job builds a service that does not import the runtime until (a). Recommendation: (b) now, because the zip is verified by the pinned hash and so is the same bytes as a release, with (a) at the first release; the build record names the source, so a reviewer sees which builds did not use the public proxy.

title: Where does an archetype's example content come from, and which settings must an author supply?
description: ST-DECL-UC01-R01 and R04 say each archetype supplies the smallest example content that checking accepts, and R05 says an empty scaffold names every setting the author must supply. Today the scaffolds of rpc-service and browser-service are refused: rpc-service needs the grpc-processes settings processes and proto_files, a proto file and a process factory package (factory/rpc.go) that imports the generated packages by the module path; browser-service needs a distinct api_prefix. The Archetype entity (ST-SUP-EN03) has no field that holds example content, and a component schema marks as required both settings the declaration must give and settings that only the running service gets (such as connection_string of postgres-adapter and issuer of jwt-auth), so checking cannot tell which settings an author must supply. Options: (a) add to the Archetype an example content field (files under the archetype folder and the settings to write into the declaration, with the module path as a placeholder), and mark in a component schema each setting the declaration must give, so that checking refuses its absence and init can name it; (b) keep the example content in Declaring's code, one case per archetype; (c) narrow R01, R04 and R05 to archetypes that can be empty, such as rest-crud. Recommendation: (a), since the UC01 notes say the archetype supplies its example content, and a registry change then needs no change to STEGO's code. Until then UC01-R01, R04-T01, R05 and the flow test stay not automated; rest-crud, which can be empty, already passes as written.

title: How does a generated service store and serve a money field of a data entity?
description: ST-DECL-INV26 and ST-DECL-UC08-R03 put a money field (type money, integer minor units, with its ISO 4217 currency) in the declaration format, and ST-DECL-UC08-R03-T02 expects stego validate to accept ST-DECL-TD04 with the money field price on the data entity Todo. Checking accepts it now. But stego validate also runs the preflight of the active components, and no output contract of the PostgreSQL adapter (ST-SUP-RC01), the REST API (ST-SUP-RC20) or the command and query runtime states how a data entity stores, sends or reads a money field. Only the ledger component states money columns (ST-SUP-RC31-OC02) and money in the OpenAPI schema (ST-SUP-RC31-OC10). So the rest-api preflight refuses the field, and R03-T02 cannot pass. Options: (a) add output contracts so that a money field of a data entity is one bigint column of minor units, its currency is the one the declaration fixes, the API sends and reads it as {amount: integer, currency: string} and refuses another currency, and the runtime carries it as money.Money (ST-SUP-RP08); (b) the same as (a), but with a char(3) currency column beside the amount, the form that ST-SUP-RC31-OC02 states for every ledger money column; (c) narrow ST-DECL-INV26 and UC08-R03 to the ledger: a data entity holds no money field, and checking refuses type money outside a ledger. Recommendation: (b). One storage form and one API form then serve the ledger and the data entities, and a stored row shows its currency without the declaration. Blocks: ST-DECL-UC08-R03-T02.

title: Does checking refuse a hot ledger account that states a minimum balance?
description: ST-DECL-UC08-R02 says that an account MAY state a minimum balance and MAY state hot, so checking accepts both on one account. But the runtime ledger refuses a hot account code with a balance limit (ST-SUP-RP08, ledger.New and ledger.DDL), because a post locks the row of an account with a limit (ST-SUP-RC31-OC07) and a hot account is never row-locked (ST-DECL-EN15). So a declaration that checking accepts would fail when the generated service starts. Options: (a) add to ST-DECL-INV26 or ST-DECL-INV27 that a hot account states no minimum balance, and checking refuses the two together, naming the account; (b) let hot win: the generator drops the limit of a hot account, with a warning; (c) let the limit win: the generator makes a hot account with a limit an ordinary account. Recommendation: (a). The author then learns of the conflict at checking (ST-BO05), and no limit is dropped without a word.

title: How must a change that adds a key to SIGNERS and signs a fill with it be stopped from qualifying its own fill?
description: The security baseline of 2026-11-11 (finding 4) found that qualification reads SIGNERS from the tree it qualifies, so one change can add a key to a SIGNERS file and sign a fill with that key, and the fill is qualified in that change's own checks. ST-EXT-TM04 says that adding a signer is a reviewed change to SIGNERS, but no record makes that review separate from the sign-off it enables. Neither fix is allowed by the records as they are: ST-EXT-SP01 and ST-EXT-UC02-R02 say the project's SIGNERS file, which is the file in the tree, and the compiler runs in a project folder that need not have git or a base ref; and no UC requirement of ST-ASR-UC02 lets the change gate refuse a change for what it does to SIGNERS. Options: (a) qualification reads SIGNERS from a base ref that the caller gives, such as stego plan --signers-ref, and the tree's file only when no ref is given; this changes ST-EXT-SP01 and ST-EXT-UC02-R02 and adds a git dependency to every user project's compile; (b) a new UC requirement of ST-ASR-UC02: the change gate refuses a change that alters a SIGNERS file and adds or changes a fill sign-off in the same tree, naming both files; such a change is split in two, or merges by the owner's review and bypass, as a change to the CI definitions does (ST-ASR-UC02-R06); (c) no code change: CODEOWNERS requires the owner's review of every SIGNERS file, which holds only when the branch rule of the base branch requires code owner review (finding 1, the owner's). Recommendation: (b), with (c) as well: it keeps qualification the same for every user project, it makes the new signer a change of its own that the owner reviews, and the gate already reads both trees. The CODEOWNERS line for **/SIGNERS is in the workflows pull request of this hardening.

title: Which step of Record what a service was built from fulfills that apply writes the record inside the service's repo?
description: ST-GEN-UC01-R05 says that apply MUST write the record inside the service's repo, beside the code it generated. Only the step ST-GEN-UC01-FL-S02 (the service author commits the record with the generated code) fulfills it, and that step invokes no command, so no technical record can build the requirement, although ST-GEN-UC01-R05-T01 is automated and passes. Options: (a) ST-GEN-UC01-FL-S01, which invokes Apply a plan (ST-GEN-CMD01), also fulfills ST-GEN-UC01-R05, and S02 keeps it too; (b) S02 also invokes Apply a plan; (c) the requirement stays proved and not built. Recommendation: (a), since apply is what writes the record in the repo and the commit only shows it.

title: How does STEGO tell the author about an upsert key with no scope on a protected entity?
description: The delta security review of PR #212 (L2, low) found that an upsert key with no scope is tenant-wide: a peer in the same tenant can take a key first, and the 409 or the update branch tells that the key exists (the known limit of ST-SUP-RP10-LC25). The orchestrator asked for a generator warning for an upsert key with no scope on an entity that has a resource type. The compiler has no warning channel: a generator can only refuse (ContextValidator) or emit files, and stego generate and stego build print no advisories. Options: (a) add an advisory channel: an optional generator interface that gives advisory lines, which the compiler collects in preflight and the commands print to stderr, with the rest-api generator giving this one; this changes what the generate use case reports. (b) Refuse an upsert key with no scope on an entity with a resource type, unless the collection states that the key is tenant-wide on purpose (a new collection setting). (c) Keep the limit and state it in ST-SUP-RC20-OC13 and the rest-crud component README only. Recommendation: (a), since other review findings also ask for warnings, and a refusal breaks declarations that are correct today.
